overview.text:
Kodaikanal, Tamil Nadu Tourism's 'Princess of Hills', sits at about 2,225 m on a plateau in the Palani Hills. British officials and missionaries set it up as a summer refuge in 1845, and it still feels like an old hill station, cool all year and often wrapped in mist.

The town centres on Kodai Lake, a star-shaped artificial lake of 1863 where you can hire rowboats and pedalos. Coaker's Walk runs along the cliff edge nearby, Bryant Park borders the lake, and the road out to Moir Point passes the pine forests, the Guna Caves and the 122 m Pillar Rocks. Further out are Berijam Lake and the solar observatory, watching the sun since 1901. The Kurinji flower blooms here only once in 12 years. April to June is the classic season; if you drive, you need an e-pass.

overview.text:
Rameswaram lies on Pamban Island, the closest point in India to Sri Lanka, and is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites. Its Ramanathaswamy Temple, one of the twelve jyotirlingas, has the longest corridor of any Hindu temple in India, about 1,200 m and lined with 1,212 carved pillars, and 22 sacred wells where pilgrims bathe. Most first bathe in the sea at Agni Theertham beside the temple.

The island is reached across the Pamban bridges: the old rail bridge of 1914 and, since April 2025, India's first vertical-lift sea bridge, beside the 1988 road bridge. At the island's tip, a road built in 2016 runs to Dhanushkodi, a town destroyed by the 1964 cyclone, and on to Arichal Munai, where two seas meet. Visit from October to March.

overview.text:
Kanyakumari, the old Cape Comorin, is the southern tip of mainland India, where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet. It takes its name from the goddess Devi Kanniyakumari, and people come to watch the sun rise and set over the sea. On full-moon days you can see sunset and moonrise at the same time.

Just offshore, ferries cross to the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the 133-ft Thiruvalluvar Statue. Since December 2024 a 77 m glass bridge, India's first over the sea, has linked the two rocks. On shore are the Gandhi Mandapam and the beach; nearby are Vattakottai Fort and quieter beaches. National Highway 44 begins here and runs 3,745 km to Srinagar. November to March is cool and pleasant.

itineraries.title: Kanyakumari in a day: sunrise, the rock and the glass bridge
itineraries.summary: Sunrise at the tip of India, the ferry to the Vivekananda Rock, the glass bridge to the Thiruvalluvar Statue, the Gandhi Mandapam and sunset.
itineraries.seoTitle: Kanyakumari in a Day: Sunrise, Vivekananda Rock & Glass Bridge
itineraries.seoDescription: A one-day Kanyakumari plan: sunrise, the ferry to the Vivekananda Rock Memorial, the glass bridge to the Thiruvalluvar Statue (8 am–4 pm), Gandhi Mandapam and sunset.

plan.overview: One full day at the southern tip of mainland India, timed around the ferry and the glass bridge's 8 am–4 pm hours.

prep.body: Thiruvananthapuram airport is 76 km away; Kanyakumari and Nagercoil stations have direct trains to most big cities.
